checks.note: getOrCreateStripeCustomer persists the caller-supplied paymentMethodId with no ownership check (and commits before the charge, since purchasePack is intentionally non-transactional), and getSavedPaymentMethod returns brand/last4/exp from stripeClient.retrievePaymentMethod(id) without ever comparing paymentMethod.getCustomer() to the caller's stripeCustomerId. The retrieve wrapper receives only the pm id so it cannot enforce ownership; the unshown sync path runs after the commit and its failures are swallowed in scheduleSubscriptionCardSync.

getOrCreateStripeCustomer's existing-customer branch saves paymentMethodId into stripe_customers before paymentGateway.chargeAndCapture runs in purchasePack, and chargeAndCapture is not wrapped in any try/catch — a declined-card exception propagates with no write-back of previousCard, which is only used in the success-path scheduleSubscriptionCardSync. The saved card is thus left as the bad one, contradicting the javadoc's "declined card is never pushed" claim.

createTier itself does no scale check, divides the raw totalPrice for pricePerSession, and returns the in-memory entity via toTierResponse(saved) — consistent with the finding — but the outcome depends on code not shown: the request DTO/controller (a @Digits-style constraint could reject 10.005 upstream) and the migration/entity mapping proving session_pack_tiers.total_price is numeric(10,2).

matches.note: R3 covers the missing upper/scale bounds causing DB overflow 500s; R4 covers the 0.00 per-session rounding violating the price CHECK — together they cover the whole defect.
R6 identifies unvalidated paymentMethodId reaching Stripe but only for the blank new-customer case, not the general format-validation gap for garbage/oversized ids on both endpoints.
